doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Hiring and managing studio musicians
summary: She chose players like Gary Chester and Artie Kaplan from demo work and dropped those who wasted time.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Oh that’s good advice. Yeah. Was there contractors involved in this that you needed to deal with?

Yeah. Some of them, but pretty much like my first husband and I were in business together at that time and we really knew, I mean for instance the strings, the people that I had known doing demos — not demos but a lot of record dates, David Nadien, who was the concertmaster for Bernstein. That happened while doing it — but you know sometimes I’d ask them to put the string section together. And the horn players I knew actually from the rock-feeling things. There were piano players, mainly ones that worked on demos that knew how to get the feel that I wanted. So it was an interesting time because with the rhythm players, they’re the new younger players. Gary Chester was the drummer. You’ve heard of his name?
And Gary said, “Just ‘cause I played strip joints, I know how to play this stuff.”
The School of Hard Knocks. Did you have any say in, “All right there’s a tenor sax solo, you know four bars here, I want Jerome Richardson.” Were you able to say that?

I would hire him. But I mean the thing was, for instance whatchacallit, baritone sax, Artie Kaplan, who did “Locomotion” and I knew Artie from demos and so forth, so if I had that commercial that had that kind of sound in it I would call Artie.
What would make a studio player not get called back?
Not having a pencil. And also questioning things that he could have figured out himself, and taking up time.
I know exactly what you mean. Yes.
There are some of those people.
Yeah you sometimes wonder if they actually knew, but they sort of wanted to put you in your place or something.
Uh huh. There was one of those.
Yup. And I didn’t call him back.
“Gee why isn’t my phone ringing anymore?” Well think about it.
